api_analysis.hypothesis: Illegal memory access is caused by passing CPU arrays (x_dims and x_strides declared on host stack) directly to the CUDA kernel. The kernel expects device pointers for these arrays, but host pointers lead to invalid global memory accesses.
evidence: In custom_ops.cu, reduce_max_4d_kernel and reduce_prod_4d_kernel dereference dims and strides as const int64_t* __restrict__ pointers, but the launcher passes host addresses from binding.cpp.
In custom_ops_binding.cpp, x_dims[4] and x_strides[4] are declared as local arrays on CPU, and their addresses are passed to launchers without copying to device memory.
Runtime error 'an illegal memory access was encountered' is consistent with dereferencing invalid host pointers inside device code.
The sanitizer log indicates the error occurs in reduce_max_kernel_forward, the first kernel launch.
changes: Modify kernels/custom_ops.cu to pass dimension and stride values as kernel parameters (by value) instead of pointers, eliminating the need for device arrays.
Update launcher signatures to accept int64_t dim0, dim1, dim2, dim3, stride0, stride1, stride2, stride3.
Update kernels/custom_ops_binding.cpp to call new launcher signatures with scalar values from x.size(i) and x.stride(i).
Ensure kernel indexing logic uses these scalar parameters correctly.
